banner.body: This policy is a draft. It is not in force and may change before it is published. Points marked [counsel] are waiting for legal review.

listingPolicy.title: How {{brand.name}} lists organisers and events
listingPolicy.summary: What we list, where the facts come from, how unclaimed pages are labelled, and how an organiser can claim, correct or remove a page.

sections.heading: What we list
paragraphs: {{brand.name}} lists independent community organisers and their events in Indian cities to help people find them.
Some pages are created by {{brand.name}} from publicly available information, such as an organiser's official website, public social profile or public event pages. These pages are marked Unclaimed.

sections.heading: Not affiliated
paragraphs: Unclaimed pages are not created, endorsed or sponsored by the organiser. The organiser has no affiliation with {{brand.name}} unless the page shows a Claimed badge.
Names and marks belong to their owners. We use them only to identify the organiser. [counsel: confirm the honest-use wording under Trade Marks Act s.30.]

sections.heading: What an unclaimed page shows
paragraphs: Unclaimed pages show only factual information: the name, city, what the organiser runs, official links and public event dates, written in our own words.
bullets: We do not use an organiser's logo, photos or descriptions unless the organiser provides or licenses them.
We do not publish personal details of the people behind an organiser beyond what identifies the organiser.
Listing an organiser does not mean it takes part in, promotes or endorses any other {{brand.name}} feature.

sections.heading: Sources and freshness
paragraphs: Each page names the public sources it was built from and when the facts were last checked. [counsel: confirm the per-field source labels before programmatic listings.]

sections.heading: Your choices as an organiser
paragraphs: You can claim your page, correct a fact, or ask us to remove your page and not list you again. Use the listing request form; each request has fixed fields, a fixed outcome and a fixed timeline.

Removal and do-not-list is open to any organisation that shows it controls an official channel (its Instagram, its website's email domain, or a letter on its letterhead). We take the page down within 24 hours of checking, delete it within 7 days and keep a minimal record so we do not list you again. [counsel: confirm the timelines and the do-not-list retention period.]

takedownPolicy.title: Notice and takedown
takedownPolicy.summary: How to ask {{brand.name}} to act on a listing: the request types, what each needs, our timelines, appeals, and how we handle misuse.

sections.heading: Scope
paragraphs: This policy explains how to ask {{brand.name}} to act on an organiser or event listing on {{brand.name}}, and how we decide.

sections.heading: How to send a request
paragraphs: To help us act quickly, please use the listing request form, which routes your request to the right team. We also accept legal notices at {{brand.support.email}} and at {{brand.operator.postalAddress}}, and route them through the same process. [counsel: confirm the form is the preferred, not the exclusive, channel for legal notices.]

sections.heading: Request types
paragraphs: Each request is one of these types. Each has fixed fields, a fixed outcome and a fixed timeline.
bullets: Claim this page. Filed by the organiser. Proof: a code sent to the official Instagram, or an email from the official domain. Outcome: the organiser manages the page. Within 2 days.
Correct a fact. Filed by the organiser or anyone, with a public link that shows the correct fact. Outcome: the fact is corrected or flagged. Within 7 days.

Remove and don't list again. Filed by the organisation. Proof: official Instagram, official email domain, or a letter on letterhead. Outcome: the page is taken down within 24 hours of checking, deleted, and a minimal record kept so it is not listed again; written confirmation. Within 7 days.

Trademark or branding. Filed by the rights holder or their agent, with the registration number, class and country, or evidence of use for an unregistered mark, and a good-faith declaration. Outcome: removed or relabelled. Within 7 days.

Copyright (photo or text). Filed by the rights holder, identifying the work, the original and the basis of ownership, with a declaration modelled on Copyright Rules 2013, Rule 75. Outcome: the material is taken down. Within 36 hours. [counsel]

Privacy or personal data. Filed by the person concerned or their nominee. We match you to what the page shows, or send a one-time code; we do not ask for identity documents by default. Outcome: personal details removed, hidden or corrected. Within 7 days. [counsel: statutory limits once the DPDP Act applies]
Impersonation. Filed by the real organiser, with official-channel proof. Outcome: the impersonating page is suspended. Within 24 hours of checking.
Court or government order. Filed by the authority. We verify the order with its issuer and act as it requires, within the time it sets. [counsel: confirm the 3-hour window for government directions]

sections.heading: Declarations
paragraphs: Every request confirms that its information is accurate and complete and that the requester is the person named or is authorised to act. Trademark, copyright and impersonation requests also confirm a good-faith belief that the use is not authorised. A false or misleading request may be refused and may lead to liability under applicable law. [counsel: wording of the declaration; we do not call it a sworn statement]

sections.heading: Timelines
paragraphs: We acknowledge every request within 24 hours and resolve it within 7 days, or within the shorter time shown for its type or required by law. [counsel: confirm against the IT Rules 2021 as amended in February 2026]

sections.heading: Counter-notice and restoration
paragraphs: When we remove content a claimed organiser supplied because of a trademark or copyright request, we tell the organiser. They may send a counter-notice that identifies the content, states their good-faith belief that it was removed by mistake, and consents to Indian jurisdiction. For copyright, content may be restored after 21 days if no court order is produced. [counsel]

sections.heading: Appeals
paragraphs: A requester or affected organiser may appeal a decision once, within 30 days, by replying with the request reference. A different reviewer decides the appeal within 7 days. Users may also appeal to the Grievance Appellate Committee where the IT Rules provide for it. [counsel]

sections.heading: What we will not do
bullets: Pay compensation or negotiate damages through the form. Legal claims go to the address above.
Disclose other people's personal data without legal process.
Act on anonymous intellectual-property complaints or on requests from people without authority.
Keep an organisation off our listings at the request of someone who cannot show they control it.
Restore a removed listing without a fresh claim by the organisation itself.

sections.heading: Misuse and repeat abuse
paragraphs: We may refuse false, abusive or repeated requests, and may stop accepting requests from people who misuse this process.

sections.heading: Records
paragraphs: We keep records of requests and of removed content as the law requires, for example 180 days under the IT Rules, and keep a minimal do-not-list record so that removed organisers are not listed again. [counsel: retention periods]

sections.heading: Grievance Officer
paragraphs: Grievance Officer: {{brand.operator.grievanceOfficer}}, for {{brand.operator.legalName}}, which operates {{brand.name}}.
Email: {{brand.support.email}}. Address: {{brand.operator.postalAddress}}.
We acknowledge complaints within 24 hours and resolve them within 7 days, or sooner where the law requires. [counsel: confirm the details to publish under IT Rules 2021, Rule 3(2), and working hours]
